analysis:
The supplied units are documentation only: a new changelog (changelog.d/glm53-native-prerequisites.md) and an edit to docs/architecture/hardware-support.md. They contain no executable code, so I could not verify any of the described implementation behavior. I found no concrete security regression and no new attack surface in the text itself.

Things the next pass should check if the GLM5Next code is reviewed:
- The changelog (lines 9 and 14) says the encrypted SSD prefix store defaults on for the pinned GLM identity and that GLM is served in coordinator-connected mode. This falls under T-041 and SEC-035. That threat entry covers default-on SSD with a per-donation adoption bound and benefit floor, and with coordinator-authored cacheSalt scoping. The bound for GLM, and cacheSalt/HMAC-tag scoping with the 30-minute TTL, should be confirmed. T-041 does not name GLM, so a threat-model update may be warranted.
- Image rows are said to decode target-only and never reuse cached prefixes (line 11). This is an assumption to verify so image-derived KV is not donated to the shared cache across tenants.
- The provider self-reports `glm5_next_v1`. The coordinator must not trust it as proof of hardware (TB-002/TB-009, ADV-001).
- MTP rectangular verification is documented as not token-identical to target-only decoding (line 12). It does not weaken confidentiality, but it changes output integrity assumptions (T-007).
- `DARKBLOOM_GLM_RECTANGULAR_VERIFY` and `DARKBLOOM_GLM_PERSISTENT_WIRED_RESIDENCY` are env switches; the former is forwarded to the launchd job. Their trust boundary (TB-003) should be checked.
- hardware-support.md lines ~98-130 and ~336-345 describe retained-root cleanup, no allocator-cache clearing on failed fences, and per-request-generation MTP binding that blocks request-ID reuse. These are memory-ownership and availability claims (T-010, T-028, T-029) and need to be matched to the code.
- Wording drift: the doc says there is no qualified GLM profile, while the changelog describes coordinator-connected serving. This is documentation consistency only.
